proposals.name: CLOSEREV — cash-close price-pressure reversion in the post-close futures-only window (16:00→16:14 ET), overnight-hold secondary variant
proposals.mechanism: Index funds, ETFs, and target-close execution algos demand liquidity at the 16:00 ET cash closing crosses; this uninformed flow is disseminated as imbalance indications from 15:45/15:50 ET and pushes the final 10 minutes plus the closing print away from equilibrium. The deviation is temporary price pressure, not information, and reverts: half shortly after the close, ~85% by next morning (Bogousslavsky-Muravyev reversal coefficient −0.85). NQ trades continuously through and after the cash close (until the 16:15 ET halt), so the reversion's earliest and cheapest expression is fading the 15:50→16:00 impulse during 16:00→16:14 — a window no existing engine or dead family has ever traded. Signal = z-scored 10-min impulse P(16:00)−P(15:50) vs its own trailing 60-day distribution; trade opposite the impulse when |z| ≥ threshold. Testable structural prediction that separates flow from data-mining: closing-auction share of volume tripled 2010→2018 (3.1%→7.5%, still growing), so effect size should be non-decreasing across the 20-year sample — a falsifiable era-trend the frozen spec includes.
proposals.literature: Bogousslavsky & Muravyev, 'Who trades at the close? Implications for price discovery and liquidity', Journal of Financial Markets 66 (2023) [https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3485840]: closing deviations revert half shortly after the close, ~85% overnight; deviations >63bp in 1% of stock-level cases; growth driven by indexing/ETFs. Cushing & Madhavan, 'Stock returns and trading at the close', JFM 3 (2000) 45-67 [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1386418199000129]: Russell-1000 AGGREGATE evidence (not just single-name) that last-5-min returns explain a disproportionate share of daily-return variance and systematically reverse after MOC imbalance publications — temporary liquidity-driven pressure at the market-wide level, which is what an index future can capture. The repo's own DR pass A (DR_V2_PASS_A_AUCTION.md rank 9, 'H6 close-overshoot evening reversion', citing Bogousslavsky-Muravyev) identified this and it was never consumed by any slate.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO loses: index-tracking funds and ETFs whose mandate is to transact AT the closing price to minimize tracking error — they are price-insensitive by construction and knowingly pay the liquidity premium (the cost passes through to fund investors as NAV drag). Target-close algo users (institutions benchmarked to the close) are the same clientele. It persists because the tracker's objective function is tracking error, not implementation cost — arbitraging it away requires overnight/post-close inventory risk that closing-auction liquidity providers cap, and the flow keeps growing structurally with passive AUM.
proposals.implementability: Fully computable today from NQ 1-min 2006-01..2026-05 (6.47M bars): both the 15:50→16:00 signal window and the 16:00→16:14 trade window exist in every era (the 16:15-16:30 ET halt post-dates and pre-dates the 2015 CME hours change on both sides; step-0 substrate audit verifies bar presence per era). Exchange-session ET timestamps handle DST natively. Bonus unique to this repo: the ~12 months of NQ tick/BBO can audit whether 1-tick-per-side slippage is realistic in the 16:00-16:15 segment specifically (quoted spread/depth), turning the thin-liquidity objection into a measurable check instead of an assumption. Pure-Python diagnostic on existing parquet; no NT8 build until promotion stage.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead families: the six price-structure reversion fades (E3-A sweep-reversal, E3-C small-gap, VA rotation, multi-day false-break, seq 368-379) and gap fade (seq 231-232). Mechanically distinct on all three axes that define those kills: (1) anchor — a scheduled flow event at a fixed clock time (cash closing cross + 15:45/15:50 imbalance dissemination), not a price level (PDH/ONH/VA/gap); (2) window — the post-cash-close futures-only segment 16:00-16:14, which no dead fade, no Solar/B-MOM engine, and no scalping Zone F family (5-120s holds) ever traded; (3) information hypothesis — documented uninformed-flow price pressure with an identified payer, not 'price moved too far from structure'. Not S2 clock-window selectivity (this is a standalone event trade, not an eligibility mask on an existing engine). Not AUCTION01-04 (market-profile value-state on tick data — same word, different concept). H6 in DR pass A was ranked but never tested, so no closure collides. The honest class-level caution stands and is listed under failure modes: modern NQ has punished every reversion form tested so far.
proposals.rho_prediction: Losing-day correlation vs SOLAR_DUAL_HTF predicted ≈ −0.10 to +0.05. Mechanically near-disjoint: the engine is flat except 14 minutes/day, and on the days it loses (late impulse CONTINUES through 16:00-16:15) the trend engine is typically on the right side of that continuation. Precedent in-repo: slate-1 fades measured losing-day corr ≈ −0.11 — the diversification direction exists for fade-shaped P&L; expectancy, not correlation, is the binding gate. Overnight-hold variant same sign of prediction with wider dispersion.
proposals.test_design: Frozen spec before any result is read (runs/<id>/spec.yaml, campaign convention). Substrate: NQ 1-min, 2006-01-03..2026-05. Step 0: era audit of 15:50-16:14 bar presence + BBO slippage audit on the 12-mo tick sample. Events: RTH days with |z| = |P16:00−P15:50| / trailing-60d-std(same 10-min move) ≥ threshold. Entry: short (long) at 16:01 open if impulse up (down); exit at 16:14 close, hard time stop, 1 contract; preregistered protective stop at 1.0× impulse magnitude. Grid (plateau-not-argmax, 3×2): z ∈ {1.5, 2.0, 2.5} × exit ∈ {16:09, 16:14}. Secondary preregistered variant (only read if primary passes): hold to next 09:30 ET open with 1.5× impulse disaster stop. Costs: $4.36/RT + 1 tick/side ($14.36 ≈ 0.72 NQ pts). Gates: N ≥ 40 per walk-forward half (2006-2015 / 2016-2026), NW t ≥ 2 pooled, both halves same sign, ≥70% of years positive, era-trend non-decreasing (the structural-growth prediction), losing-day corr ≤ 0.25 vs daily Solar ledgers, max-single-event-loss and CVaR5 reported, event-loss atlas cross-referenced against post-close earnings weeks.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Index-level netting: B-M's >63bp deviations are single-name; cross-sectional netting means NDX-level deviations are usually far smaller — the effect may be super-cost only on rare large-imbalance days, shrinking N below 40. (2) The six-fade graveyard: the strongest prior against — modern NQ has paid continuation and punished every tested fade; if breakout fuel dominates even the post-close segment, this dies the same death (that would itself be new information: the continuation regime extends past the cash close). (3) Post-close scheduled news: NDX heavyweights release earnings 16:01-16:30 ET (MSFT/META/TSLA ~16:05) — a 16:00-16:14 hold has genuine event-gap left-tail; mitigated by the impulse-proportional stop, reported explicitly, but not fully removable without an earnings calendar the repo lacks. (4) Thin post-close liquidity: 1-tick slip may be optimistic exactly on the largest events (the BBO audit measures this; if measured spread kills it, that is a clean pre-outcome kill). (5) Decay/crowding: the paper is 2023-published and closing-auction liquidity provision is an established industry; residual index-level edge may already live inside the spread. (6) Cushing-Madhavan's aggregate evidence is 1997-98 — a quarter-century old; its market-wide reversal magnitude may not have survived decimalization, let alone 2020s auction design.

proposals.name: EODREV — end-of-day hedging-flow overshoot, next-day reversal (fade the last-30-min move conditional on rest-of-day agreement)
proposals.mechanism: Leveraged/inverse ETF re-leveraging and option market-makers' gamma hedging generate mandatory, price-insensitive, same-direction-as-the-day flow concentrated in the last ~30 minutes (Cheng-Madhavan mechanics: BOTH long- and inverse-LETFs buy after up days, sell after down days, demand ∝ |day return| × AUM × leverage). Baltussen et al. document the resulting last-30-min continuation across 60+ futures AND that it 'reverts over the next days' — i.e., the late-day move is partly pressure, not information. MOM01 already tested (and locally killed) the continuation leg on NQ. This proposal trades the OTHER leg, never tested in-repo on any sample: when the 15:30→16:00 move is large AND agrees in sign with the open→15:30 move (the configuration where mandated flow is maximal), fade it — enter opposite at 16:10-16:14, exit next-day 09:30 open (primary) or next-day 15:30 (secondary). This is liquidity provision to a mechanically forced flow, conditioned on the REALIZED late move, not a prediction of it.
proposals.literature: Cheng & Madhavan, 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds', Journal of Investment Management 7(4) 2009 [https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1539120]: closed-form rebalancing demand, always same-direction as the index day return, concentrated near the close. Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens, 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum', JFE 142(1) 2021, 377-403 [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X21001598]: 60+ futures 1974-2020, last-30-min continuation economically and statistically significant, linked to gamma/LETF hedging demand, AND the returns 'revert over the next days' — the documented basis for the reversal leg. Adversarial citations loaded honestly: Ivanov & Lenkey, 'Do leveraged ETFs really amplify late-day returns and volatility?', JFM 2018 [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1386418117302604] — capital flows offset rebalancing demand; after controls the late-day impact is economically insignificant. Gao-Han-Li-Zhou's related intraday-momentum effect (JFE 2018) shows documented post-publication out-of-sample disappearance ('Understanding intraday momentum strategies', JFFM 2022 replication).
proposals.economic_driver: WHO loses: LETF sponsors rebalance mechanically regardless of price (cost passed to LETF holders as volatility decay — a documented, tolerated product feature), and short-gamma option market-makers hedge mechanically into the close. Both flows are mandated by product structure/risk limits, not discretion, which is why the pressure can persist despite being known; the counterparty earning it bears overnight inventory risk, which is exactly what this engine prices. NDX-specific relevance: TQQQ/SQQQ complex (launched 2010) is among the largest LETF pools in the world and tracks this exact index.
proposals.implementability: Fully computable from NQ 1-min: open→15:30 return, 15:30→16:00 return, trailing vol scaling, entry 16:10-16:14 (pre-halt), exit next 09:30 or 15:30 — all bars exist across the 20-year sample. Event frequency ~1-2/week at a top-quintile |day-move| threshold → N in the hundreds over 20 years, with a preregistered era split at 2010 (TQQQ/SQQQ launch) because the mechanism's AUM base barely existed 2006-2009. Python-only diagnostic on existing parquet.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest closures, each named and distinguished: (1) MOM01 CLEAN_NULL — that was the CONTINUATION leg (does ROD predict the last 30 min), on the 4.4-yr 3-min substrate; this trades the reversal of the realized late move, a different conditional, different window, different sample (20-yr 1-min), and MOM01's own report scoped itself as 'closing diagnostic' on replication+redundancy, not on next-day reversal. (2) Killed unconditional overnight-drift cheap kill (slate 1) — this is conditional and direction-symmetric, not an unconditional overnight hold. (3) B1 overnight-long-premium (PARKED, not proposable) — B1 is unconditional and long-only; this is a two-sided conditional fade; on big-down-day nights its long position partially resembles B1's, so the spec preregisters an orthogonality read vs the B1 ledger. (4) Not Baltussen-style intraday momentum as an information hypothesis: the trade is explicitly anti-momentum liquidity provision against a documented mandated flow. (5) Not the six price-structure fades: anchor is a flow event scaled by AUM×|return|, not a price level, and the hold is overnight, a horizon none of the six traded.
proposals.rho_prediction: Losing-day correlation vs SOLAR_DUAL_HTF predicted ≈ −0.10 to +0.10. On its losing nights (the day's trend CONTINUES overnight) the long-biased trend engine is typically positioned with that continuation, so losses anti-align. The shared-loss scenario is narrow: overnight V-reversals immediately after days where Solar was also fighting the move. Flag for the tail gate rather than the corr gate: fading large down days = long overnight into potential crash continuation — the corr number should pass while the left tail does the real gating work.
proposals.test_design: Frozen spec before results. Substrate: NQ 1-min 2006-2026. Events: RTH days with |r(open→15:30)| ≥ 1.25× trailing-60d std AND sign(r15:30→16:00) == sign(r open→15:30) AND |r(15:30→16:00)| ≥ its own trailing 1.0σ. Entry: 16:10 close, direction opposite the day move, 1 contract. Exit: next 09:30 ET open (primary); grid (plateau, 3×2): day-move threshold ∈ {1.0σ, 1.25σ, 1.5σ} × exit ∈ {next 09:30, next 15:30}. Preregistered disaster stop: 2.0× the trailing overnight-gap σ. Costs: $4.36/RT + 1 tick/side. Gates: N ≥ 40 per half, NW t ≥ 2, walk-forward halves (2006-2015/2016-2026) same sign, ≥70% of years positive, post-2010 era effect ≥ pre-2010 (AUM prediction), losing-day corr ≤ 0.25 vs Solar ledgers, B1-ledger orthogonality read, CVaR5 of overnight holds + worst-night atlas (must include Feb-2018, Mar-2020, Aug-2024 style nights) as a hard tail gate.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) The premise is contested in print: Ivanov-Lenkey show capital flows offset LETF rebalancing and late-day impact becomes economically insignificant after controls — if they are right for NDX, there is no pressure to revert. (2) MOM01's local clean null on the continuation leg is soft evidence the NQ pressure footprint is weak in 2022-2026; a null here would rhyme with that. (3) Documented post-publication decay in the adjacent Gao et al. effect (out-of-sample disappearance after 2013 sample end) — this family is well-known to practitioners since ~2018-2021. (4) Structural left tail: fading large down days overnight is short-crash-insurance; a single 2020-style continuation night can erase months — the disaster stop and CVaR gate are load-bearing, and failing the tail gate kills the family regardless of mean. (5) Gamma-demand sign is unobservable without options data (killed GAMMA00 lane): the |day-move| proxy assumes dealers are net short gamma, which post-2022 0DTE market structure may have changed. (6) Pre-2010 sample dilution: if the effect only exists post-2010, the effective sample is 16 years and the era gate must carry more weight.

proposals.name: LIQREV-1: Stress-gated daily-horizon liquidity-provision reversal (Nagel/CGW conditional snapback engine)
proposals.mechanism: The expected return to SUPPLYING liquidity is strongly state-dependent: near zero (or negative after costs) in calm markets, large and positive when volatility/stress is high and intermediary capital withdraws. Concretely: after a bottom-quantile down day (or top-quantile up day) that occurs INSIDE a high-stress state (trailing realized-vol percentile high, optionally high relative volume per CGW), the next 1-2 sessions carry a positive expected reversal component as risk-averse liquidity providers are paid to absorb deleveraging/margin-driven flow. The tradable claim is the INTERACTION (stress x extreme-day -> reversal), not unconditional reversion — the unconditional version is already locally falsified and the proposal predicts ~zero in the calm state, which doubles as a built-in mechanism check.
proposals.literature: Nagel, 'Evaporating Liquidity', RFS 25(7) 2012 (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/25/7/2005/1602153; NBER w17653 https://www.nber.org/papers/w17653): short-term reversal returns = returns to liquidity provision; strongly predictable by VIX; conditional Sharpe rises enormously in turmoil; ~1%/day during LTCM 1998, 2000-01, 2007-09 episodes, even for industry-portfolio reversal that earns ~nothing unconditionally. Campbell-Grossman-Wang, QJE 108(4) 1993 (https://academic.oup.com/qje/article-abstract/108/4/905/1899978): INDEX-level daily return autocorrelation declines with volume — high-volume declines are more likely to revert (risk-averse market makers accommodating non-informational flow); this is aggregate-index, time-series evidence, directly on point for a single-future implementation. Khandani-Lo (J. Fin. Markets 2011): contrarian profits collapse secularly but spike in stress. Brunnermeier-Pedersen, RFS 2009 (margin/funding spirals): why it persists — arbitrage capital is forced out exactly when the premium is largest. Local corroboration in-repo: SMV2K complementarity paradox — the killed intraday fades earned +$306/+$401 on champion bottom-decile days with losing-day corr ~ -0.11 while losing money unconditionally; exactly the state-dependence this literature predicts.
proposals.economic_driver: Who loses: forced sellers/buyers — margin-called leveraged funds, vol-target and risk-parity deleveragers, LETF end-of-day rebalancers, retail capitulation — who demand immediacy during stress and pay a concession. Why it persists: liquidity-provider balance-sheet constraints bind precisely in stress (funding spirals); HFT liquidity provision, which killed the calm-state premium post-2000 (Chordia et al. attenuation evidence), withdraws inventory-bearing capacity in exactly these states. The premium is compensation for bearing continuation/left-tail risk when nobody else will — it cannot be arbitraged away without someone holding that risk overnight.
proposals.implementability: Fully implementable today: NQ 1-min 2006-01..2026-05 (20 years) collapsed to a daily RTH ledger. Stress state = trailing 5-day realized vol (from 1-min RTH returns) percentile-ranked vs trailing 252 sessions; relative volume from bar volume. ~20 years includes 2007-09, 2010, 2011, 2015-16, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024-25 stress clusters — solving the killed fades' 2022-26-only sample problem. Entry/exit at 15:58 ET market orders; overnight hold of 1 NQ (or MNQ for granularity); skip roll days (back-adjusted merge handles pricing). Daily Solar ledgers exist for the correlation gate. Cost 0.31bp of current notional ($14.36/RT vs ~$470k notional) — a 5-10bp conditional effect clears it by an order of magnitude, so the test is a power/existence question, not a cost-engineering question.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead families, and why this is distinct: (1) six price-structure reversion fades + E3-A/E3-C (seq 368-370, 377-379) — all intraday 3-min-substrate, level/structure-anchored (PDH/ONH/IB/value-area/VWAP), UNCONDITIONAL on liquidity state, 2022-26 only; this is daily-horizon, close-to-close, no price structure, 20-year sample, and claims positive expectancy ONLY in the stress state (predicts ~zero in calm — consistent with, not contradicted by, those kills). (2) Gap fade (seq 231-232) — overnight-gap trigger, stopless left tail; no gap variable here, and tail-concentration gates are inherited from that failure. (3) VR/ER trend-quality states (0/12 cells) — those targeted next-session SOLAR PnL as a conditioning overlay, not standalone reversal expectancy. (4) Auction M2/M3 value-distance reversion — tick-markout horizons on 37 sessions, sub-cost (Case B); different horizon, state, and sample by orders of magnitude. (5) B1 overnight long premium (PARKED, not touched) — B1 is unconditional calendar-window long; this trades ~10-15% of days, both directions, conditional. (6) M1 vol-seasonal rescale / M5 ATR family — incumbent threshold engineering inside Solar, different layer entirely. Not intraday momentum, not directional-change trend capture: it is an anti-continuation claim in a defined state. Honest residual risk: it IS a member of the broader 'reversion' class the repo marks INFERENCE-dead; the frozen calm-state control and interaction test make this a falsification of that inference at a new horizon/sample rather than a re-spec of any killed config.
proposals.rho_prediction: Losing-day correlation vs the long-biased Solar trend engine predicted <= 0.10 and plausibly negative: the engine is flat ~85-90% of days (structural zero correlation), and when active it earns on sharp snapback/whipsaw days — the exact days trend capture gives back. Locally documented analog: -0.11 losing-day corr for stress-day fades (SMV2K). It also matches the recorded design target that future Engine-3 work should be variance-timing/tail-shaping in high-variance whipsaw weeks, not loss-avoidance.
proposals.test_design: Preregister frozen spec BEFORE any outcome read (runs/<id>/spec.yaml). Substrate: daily ledger from NQ 1-min, 2006-01-03..2026-05 (dev window may reserve 2024-26 per campaign convention). State: stress_t = 5d realized vol >= 90th pct of trailing 252 sessions (primary); secondary CGW axis: relative volume >= 80th pct. Signal: session close-to-close return in bottom (long) or top (short) quintile of trailing 63 sessions. Trade: enter 15:58 ET, exit next session 15:58 (1-day hold; 2-day hold as one plateau axis), 1 contract, no intraday stop but skip roll days; both sides reported separately. Costs: $4.36/RT + 1 tick/side = $14.36/RT. Gates (all frozen): N >= 300 events; net/trade day-clustered bootstrap CI_lo > 0; positive sign in >= 5 of 7 named stress clusters; calm-state control (same quintile trigger, stress=0) NOT significantly positive — if it is, the state variable is not doing the work and the family stops; top-1% of trades <= 50% of net and preregistered worst-trade/ES5 bounds (inherited from the B02 failure signature); 3x3 plateau (vol pct 85/90/95 x quintile 20/25/30) must be uniformly positive — plateau not argmax; losing-day corr <= 0.25 vs Solar daily ledger; combined-portfolio right-tail retention check. Constants are literature defaults, declared untuned.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Left tail: sustained cascades (Oct-2008-style consecutive down days) produce repeated losing longs; the strategy is short-vol-of-vol in the worst weeks — the ES5/tail-concentration gates exist to catch exactly this, and a fat left tail is grounds for kill even with positive mean. (2) Documented decay: unconditional short-term reversal profits collapsed post-2000 as HFT replaced specialists (Chordia et al.); if the CONDITIONAL premium has also been competed away on a hyper-liquid index future, the 2010s-2020s clusters will be flat and only 2008 carries the result — the per-cluster sign gate makes this visible and fatal. (3) Cross-sectional-to-time-series transfer risk: Nagel's construction is cross-sectional equity; index-level reversal is far weaker (CGW is index-level but 1962-88 — ancient); honest prior is a small effect that may not clear significance with N~300-500. (4) Event confound: stress days cluster around macro releases/FOMC — must check the effect is not a re-expression of the closed 08:30/pre-FOMC axes (event-day exclusion as robustness read). (5) Regime dependence: modern NQ punished every tested reversion form 2022-26; if the interaction term is flat there specifically, the engine may be dead-forward even if alive 2006-2020 — chronological stability gate covers this. Failure probability is material; the compensating factor is that the test is cheap, fully preregistrable, and falsifies (or confirms) the repo's own class-level INFERENCE with a 4x larger stress sample than any prior fade test.

proposals.name: LIQSTATE-0: BBO-year-certified low-frequency liquidity proxies as a 20-year market-quality state variable (measurement/certification study, enabler not engine)
proposals.mechanism: Direct answer to the lane's tick/BBO question. The ~12-month tick/BBO year cannot be a chronology-compatible signal source (U2: 12mo vs 4.4yr LOYO; U9B: underpowered null) — but it CAN serve as a one-time fidelity certifier for OHLC-derived liquidity proxies that DO have 20 years of chronology. Compute candidate low-frequency estimators (EDGE, Corwin-Schultz, Abdi-Ranaldo, Roll autocovariance, Amihud |r|/volume) from the 1-min/daily bars; compute ground-truth daily effective spread, time-weighted quoted spread, and top-of-book depth from the BBO year; certify which proxy (if any) tracks the true liquidity state day-by-day. A certified proxy becomes a legitimate 20-year market-quality state for LIQREV-1's secondary axis and any future engine; a clean failure closes the 'liquidity proxies from OHLCV' question permanently with evidence instead of assumption.
proposals.literature: Corwin-Schultz, 'A Simple Way to Estimate Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily High and Low Prices', JF 2012 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/227374881); Abdi-Ranaldo, 'A Simple Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily Close, High, and Low Prices', RFS 2017 (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2725981); Ardia-Guidotti-Kroencke, 'Efficient estimation of bid-ask spreads from open, high, low, and close prices' (EDGE), JFE 2024 (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X24001399). All three validate against high-frequency TAQ benchmarks with documented high correlations for equities — and documented caveats: the estimators are biased in ways that co-vary with volatility, and perform worst exactly where spreads are pinned near the tick floor, which is the honest central risk on NQ.
proposals.economic_driver: None claimed — this is a measurement study, not an alpha proposal. Its value is decision-information: it either unlocks a 20-year liquidity state (materially upgrading LIQREV-1 and any future liquidity-conditional family) or produces a definitive, cheap negative that stops future OHLCV-liquidity-proxy proposals cold.
proposals.implementability: Trivially implementable today, zero new data: proxies from existing NQ 1-min/daily bars; ground truth from the existing ~12 months tick/BBO (grid1s substrate already built by scalping_lab, plus the 39 ES tick sessions as an out-of-instrument sanity check). Purely offline analytics; no NT8, no orders, no protected pools.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest prior work: U2 (tick/BBO 'chronology-incompatible' — this DESIGN sidesteps that verdict because the deliverable state variable has 20-year chronology; BBO is used only cross-sectionally in time to certify fidelity, not as a signal); U9B (microstructure entry-alpha null — this computes no entry alpha at all); R5 (OHLCV microstructure PROXIES for order flow — R5 tested proxies as alpha features against trade outcomes and found tail-blind bulk signals; this tests proxies against MEASURED liquidity, a question R5 never asked and could not ask before the BBO year existed); DOM01/DATA03 (PAUSED — untouched; no depth history is used or needed). Not OHLCV single-feature MINING: there is no outcome variable in the study, hence no data-mining surface — the target is measured spread/depth, not P&L.
proposals.rho_prediction: n/a — no P&L stream. Downstream: if certification passes, the resulting state variable inherits its correlation properties from whatever engine consumes it (for LIQREV-1 the prediction stands as given there).
proposals.test_design: Frozen prereg: over the BBO overlap window (~250 sessions), compute daily {EDGE, CS, AR, Roll, Amihud} from bars and daily {trade-weighted effective spread, time-weighted quoted spread, mean top-of-book depth, depth imbalance dispersion} from BBO. Certification gates (frozen): daily Spearman >= 0.5 vs effective spread (or vs a depth-state composite) for at least one proxy, stable sign and >= 0.35 in each of 4 disjoint quarters, and rank agreement on the top-decile 'stressed' days >= 70% (the tail is what a stress gate consumes). Secondary discriminant-validity check: the winning proxy must NOT be explainable by realized vol alone (partial Spearman vs effective spread controlling for 5d realized vol must stay > 0.2) — otherwise the honest conclusion is 'use realized vol, proxies add nothing'. Output: a certified (or refuted) 20-year daily liquidity-state series committed as infrastructure, mirroring the U0 state-table pattern.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Most likely failure, stated plainly: NQ RTH quoted spread is pinned at 1 tick the vast majority of the time, so true liquidity variation lives in DEPTH, which OHLC estimators cannot see — the discriminant-validity gate will then correctly report that the proxies are just noisy volatility restatements, and the study closes negative. That outcome still answers the lane's question ('can the BBO year make anything usable as a state?' -> no, beyond realized vol we already have). (2) The BBO year covers only 2025-26 regimes; certification is regime-local and says nothing about proxy fidelity in 2008 — must be disclosed on the output series. (3) Estimator bias co-varies with volatility (documented in the 2024 JFE paper) — the exact confound the partial-correlation gate targets. (4) Scope creep risk: this must not silently become alpha-mining on the BBO year; the prereg contains no outcome variable by construction.

proposals.name: TOM-FLOW: Turn-of-month institutional cash-cycle long window (T-1 through T+3)
proposals.mechanism: The monthly payment cycle forces price-inelastic trading: pensions/mutual funds raise cash before month-end obligations (payrolls, benefit payments, redemptions settling under T+3/T+2/T+1), then new-month contributions (401k payroll cycle, pension contribution dates) are mechanically reinvested in the first days of the month. The reinvestment pressure concentrates the equity premium into the ~4-day turn-of-month window. This is an ALWAYS-LONG, unconditional calendar flow harvest — not a fade of anything, not a sign-flipping rebalance signal.
proposals.literature: Lakonishok & Smidt, RFS 1988 (DJIA 1897-1986: TOM 4-day return 0.473% vs ~0.35% for the average full month). McConnell & Xu, Financial Analysts Journal 2008 (CRSP 1926-2005 and separately 1987-2005: essentially ALL excess equity return accrues in TOM = last trading day + first 3; holds in S&P 500 futures; 30+ of 34 countries; not explained by risk, size, or news calendar). Carchano & Tornero (S&P 500 futures 1991-2008: TOM is the ONLY calendar effect statistically and economically significant and persistent in futures). Mechanism paper: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, 'Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs', RFS 2020, 33(1):75-111 — global evidence that the monthly payment cycle raises the cost of debt and equity capital at month-end key dates and that mutual funds/institutions demonstrably suffer from liquidity-motivated trading. Decay evidence exists and is mixed: Maberly & Waggoner (2000) claim disappearance in S&P futures post-1990; Dzhabarov & Ziemba (2010) find it alive 1993-2009 but with days migrating earlier due to anticipation. Sources: papers.ssrn.com/abstract=917884, academic.oup.com/rfs/article/33/1/75/5494694, quantpedia.com/strategies/turn-of-the-month-in-equity-indexes.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO loses: institutions whose trading calendar is contractual, not discretionary — funds that must hold cash at month-end and must reinvest month-start inflows regardless of price. They pay a liquidity premium to whoever provides balance-sheet at exactly those dates. WHY it persists: the flow is scheduled and inelastic (agency/mandate constraints), and Etula et al document that arbitrage capital against it is limited precisely when the flow arrives — the anomaly is compensation for providing month-end liquidity, so it decays slowly rather than vanishing on publication.
proposals.implementability: Fully implementable today: pure day-of-month flags on the NQ 1-min 2006-01..2026-05 substrate (6.47M bars, ~245 month-turns, ~980 day-events). No new data of any kind. Entry/exit at RTH closes computable from the 1-min bars; costs at the frozen C1 ($4.36/RT + 1 tick/side).
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead family: seq 379 month-end flow tilt (SMV2P slate 2) — that spec was a CONDITIONAL SIGN-FLIPPING FADE (direction = opposite of NQ MTD return, last 2 trading days only, RTH-only) and died ~zero. TOM-FLOW is mechanically distinct: always-long (never conditions on MTD sign), and 3 of its 4 days (T+1..T+3) have ZERO window overlap with 379. The repo's own Wave-4 pass D3#3 deferred (did not kill) exactly this candidate and required 'an explicit zero-correlation check against the killed signal' — that check is preregistered here (report signal correlation on overlapping days; robustness cell: effect must survive dropping T-1 entirely). Day-of-week kill (scalping P4): not a naming trick — TOM is day-of-MONTH anchored to a documented payment cycle; frozen independence check: the effect must not be carried by any single weekday cell. B1 overnight-long-premium (PARKED, not proposable): handled by a frozen decomposition arm — if the TOM edge is entirely the overnight component, verdict routes to 'B1 in a calendar mask — not a new engine' and the proposal FAILS by its own rule; it only stands if the calendar conditioning adds expectancy beyond the unconditional overnight baseline (which the repo already measured as ~zero-drift: slate-1 overnight-drift kill actually HELPS here — unconditional overnight is dead locally, so any TOM-window premium is calendar-specific by construction).
proposals.rho_prediction: Active ~4 of 21 trading days per month, flat otherwise. On active days it is long, same side as the Solar long tilt, so same-day covariance is positive when both are on — but 85% dilution and Solar's losing days being chop/whipsaw days (spread across the month, not TOM-concentrated) predict losing-day correlation ~0.10-0.15. This is the slate's weakest gate risk and is measured against the actual daily Solar ledgers before any promotion; a TOM-window crash (e.g., Feb-2020 month-end) hitting a Solar losing streak is the failure cell.
proposals.test_design: Frozen spec: long 1 NQ from RTH close of the month's second-to-last trading day, exit RTH close of the 3rd trading day of the new month (4 trading days held, overnights included — disclosed NOT day-only, per the 378 precedent); no stop (right-tail open, left tail = 4 days of unhedged beta, disclosed). Window 2006-01..2026-05; walk-forward halves 2006-2016 / 2016-2026 must agree in sign; sign consistency across all four 5-year blocks (driver existed the whole sample, so 'structural or die' applies). Gates: after-cost net > 0 with CI_lo > 0 at C1; t_NW >= 2 on the TOM-minus-matched-non-TOM-4-day-window difference; plateau over window shifts {T-2..T+2, T-1..T+3, T0..T+4} all same sign; preregistered arms: (a) overnight-vs-RTH decomposition with the B1-mask fail rule, (b) drop-T-1 robustness, (c) weekday-cell independence, (d) correlation-vs-killed-379-signal report, (e) losing-day corr vs Solar ledgers <= 0.25. N ~ 980 day-events / ~245 window-events.
proposals.failure_modes: 1) Anticipation migration: Dzhabarov-Ziemba document the days shifting earlier — a fixed window can miss a moved effect (plateau cells partially cover this). 2) T+1 settlement (May 2024) compresses the cash-raising timeline — the last ~2 years may show a shifted pattern; too little data to re-fit, disclosed. 3) Old-regime concentration: if the premium lives mostly pre-2013 the WF gate kills it — Maberly-Waggoner say exactly this for futures; this is the single most likely kill outcome. 4) B1-mask: the edge may be entirely overnight carry — auto-fail by frozen rule. 5) Unstopped 4-day beta left tail (month-end Oct-2008, Feb/Mar-2020 turns) — right-tail-safe but LEFT-tail-exposed; concentration gates (top-1% share, worst-event bounds per the B02 precedent) must be part of any Stage-2 spec. 6) Correlation gate: long-only calendar beta vs a long-biased trend engine may breach rho <= 0.25 on crash-overlap months.

proposals.name: TERMFLOW: Calendar-flagged terminal-flow continuation into the 16:00 cash close
proposals.mechanism: On a small set of calendar-flagged sessions (month-end, quarter-end, monthly OPEX, quad-witching, index-rebalance effective dates), benchmark-tracked passive funds MUST execute at the 4pm cash closing auction (NAV/tracking anchored to the close). Their orders are price-inelastic and partially telegraphed (exchange imbalance feeds from ~15:50), so the pre-close drift on flagged days is flow, not information, and continues into the close instead of reverting. Trade: on flagged days only, direction = sign of the 15:30->15:50 NQ move, enter 15:50, exit at the 15:59/16:00 cash close. The INFORMATION is the calendar (who is forced to trade today), not the price path — on unflagged days the same rule is already known to be dead on NQ (MOM01 CLEAN_NULL), which becomes the built-in control.
proposals.literature: Cushing & Madhavan, Journal of Financial Markets 2000, 'Stock returns and trading at the close' — systematic price pressure in the final 15 minutes tied to index-linked order flow; returns strongly related to close imbalances. Bogousslavsky & Muravyev, Journal of Financial Markets 2023, 'Who trades at the close?' — closing auctions grew from 3.1% (2010) to 7.5%+ (2018) of volume, and closing volume SPIKES specifically on index-rebalancing days and end-of-month days (the exact flag set proposed); they also document that auction-price deviations revert almost completely — which is why the frozen leg here is the 15:50->close continuation of anticipatory flow, not holding through/after the auction print. Chinco & Sammon (JFE 2024, passive ownership ~2x measured share; index funds trade the close on reconstitution days) and Harris & Gurel (JF 1986, price pressure from index flows) anchor the flow-inelasticity premise. Sources: papers.ssrn.com/abstract=3485840, econpapers.repec.org/article/eeefinmar/v_3a66_3ay_3a2023.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO loses: passive/benchmark-tracked funds, knowingly — they accept close-execution impact cost as the price of tracking fidelity (tracking error at the close is career risk; impact cost is not). This is one of the best-documented persistent wealth transfers in market microstructure, and it has GROWN with passive AUM — the mechanism predicts a rising effect over 2006-2026, the opposite signature of the campaign's dead-old-regime failures.
proposals.implementability: Fully implementable today: NQ 1-min 2006-2026; all flags are pure public calendar arithmetic (last trading day of month/quarter; 3rd Fridays; quad-witching Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec; NDX annual reconstitution 3rd Friday Dec — note that flag alone was cheap-killed as a STANDALONE at N=4 in slate 5 and here is only one member of a pooled family, disclosed). ~28-32 events/yr, ~600 events over 20 years. No imbalance feed exists in our data — the 15:30->15:50 move is the flow-direction proxy, disclosed as such. Cost hurdle trivially clearable in points terms: $14.36 full RT ~ 0.72 NQ pts vs documented flagged-day pre-close drifts of several bps (5 bps of NQ ~ 10+ pts).
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead families, in order: (1) MOM01 Baltussen-style intraday momentum, CLEAN_NULL — the decisive distinction: MOM01 is the ALL-DAYS version and its null is preregistered here as the control baseline; TERMFLOW's claim is a flagged-day DIFFERENCE, and the gate requires flagged-minus-matched-unflagged significance, so it cannot pass by re-expressing generic intraday momentum. (2) Killed seq 398 post-expiration gamma-unclamp breakout — different day (next session), different object (direction-neutral vol expansion); TERMFLOW is same-day directional flow into the close; the repo's own D3#2 pass entry rated the standalone terminal-flow candidate 'strong candidate, low dedup' and explicitly deferred it 'to a future slate if 398 fails' — 398 failed, so this is the repo's own designated next step, not a re-spec. (3) B-MOM (intraday momentum engine, E2): preregistered incremental-info check — if B-MOM already holds the same direction at 15:50 on >70% of flagged events, TERMFLOW adds nothing and fails. (4) The 2026-08-09 scout's 'no clear NQ mechanism from closing-auction literature' note: that pass evaluated clock-phase liquidity U-shapes (already encoded in session_phase); the calendar-flag information axis was not what it assessed. (5) S2 clock-window selectivity kill: TERMFLOW is not a clock window — the 15:50-16:00 window is identical on all days; the flag varies, and the flag is the hypothesis.
proposals.rho_prediction: Near-zero losing-day correlation vs Solar: active ~10 minutes on ~30 days/yr, direction symmetric (short flagged-day sell-flow as readily as long buy-flow), P&L per event small relative to Solar's daily swings. Right-tail-safe: trades WITH observed flow, time-boxed to 10 minutes, always flat by 16:00 — no overnight, no unbounded adverse leg.
proposals.test_design: Frozen spec: flag set = {last trading day of month, last trading day of quarter, 3rd-Friday monthly OPEX, quad-witching Fridays, NDX Dec reconstitution effective day}; on flagged days, if |15:30->15:50 return| > 0, enter at 15:51 bar open in that direction, exit 15:59 bar close (16:00 ET cash close); one event/day; costs C1 with 1-tick slip/side. Window 2006-01..2026-05. Gates: after-cost net > 0, CI_lo > 0; t_NW >= 2 vs zero AND vs the matched-unflagged control (same rule on N random unflagged days, prereg seed); N >= 400 traded; WF halves 2006-2016/2016-2026 same sign, with the preregistered structural prediction that the second half is STRONGER (passive-growth regime — failing that prediction is reportable but not a kill if both halves are positive); plateau: entry {15:45, 15:50, 15:52} x lookback-start {15:30, 15:35, 15:40} all same sign; descriptive per-flag subfamily readout with NO subfamily selection (pooled result is the only gate — no cherry-picking OPEX vs month-end after the read); B-MOM direction-overlap cell as above; losing-day corr vs Solar ledgers <= 0.25.
proposals.failure_modes: 1) Futures lead the cash: NQ may fully embed the anticipated MOC flow by 15:50 — the drift lives 15:30-15:50 and the tradable residual is zero; this is the most likely kill. 2) Bogousslavsky-Muravyev's near-complete reversion of auction deviations implies the last minutes can be systematically FADE-shaped — the continuation sign could be significantly negative (which would itself be a finding, per the E3-A precedent, but the engine dies). 3) Direction proxy misclassification (no imbalance feed) halves the effective signal. 4) Flag heterogeneity: NDX/SPX index options settle at the OPEN on expiration Fridays, so the OPEX close flow is weaker/different than month-end flow — pooling dilutes; disclosed, and the pooled gate is kept anyway to prevent post-hoc selection. 5) MOM01's clean null is an honest bad prior for ANY intraday continuation on NQ; if the flagged-day difference is real but small, a ~600-event sample at 10-minute horizon may still be underpowered against t_NW >= 2.

proposals.name: QREBAL: Quarter-end 60/40 mechanical-rebalancing pressure with bond-leg conditioning
proposals.mechanism: Multi-asset mechanical rebalancers (target-date funds ~$4T, pensions, 60/40 mandates) trade AGAINST the quarter's stock-minus-bond relative move on a schedule concentrated at quarter-end (calendar rebalancers) or just after large divergences (threshold rebalancers). When stocks massively outperformed bonds intraquarter, predictable equity SELLING hits the last day(s) of the quarter; after equity crashes, predictable equity BUYING (the Mar-2020 archetype, street-estimated in the hundreds of billions). Trade WITH the predicted flow: position on the last 2 trading days of quarter in the direction opposite the quarter's stock-bond gap, only when |gap| exceeds a threshold (no gap = no flow = no trade), exit by close of the first day of the new quarter.
proposals.literature: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone, 'The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing', NBER w33554 (2025) / SSRN 5122748: rebalancing by calendar and threshold funds generates predictable price pressure — equity-overweight signals predict a ~17 bps equity decline over the next day; estimated ~$16B/yr aggregate cost to rebalancers; both monthly and quarterly schedules documented, threshold triggers clustering after large divergences. Supporting: Etula et al RFS 2020 (month-end institutional flow); practitioner documentation of quarter-end pension flow estimates. Sources: nber.org/papers/w33554, papers.ssrn.com/abstract=5122748.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO loses: the mechanical rebalancers themselves — Harvey et al quantify the $16B/yr transfer and show mandate fidelity (not execution alpha) is the fiduciary objective, so the flow persists despite being front-runnable. The flow SCALES with mechanical-rebalancer AUM, which grew ~10x since 2006 (target-date fund adoption post-PPA-2006) — a genuinely different economic hypothesis from the killed seq-379 spec, with the opposite regime prediction.
proposals.implementability: PARTIAL — the only proposal in this slate needing anything beyond the frozen substrate: the signal requires a bond leg, and the repo has NO Treasury futures data. Free public daily Treasury yields (FRED DGS10, or Treasury.gov par yields; duration-approximated bond total return) would suffice — analogous in spirit to the 'hardcoded public event calendar' precedent from SMV2X, but it IS a new (free) data dependency and the campaign may rule it outside 'our data today'. Without a bond leg the signal degenerates into NQ-MTD-sign — which is exactly the killed 379 — so there is no fallback: no bond leg, no proposal. Events: ~80 quarter-ends in 2006-2026, ~40-55% clearing a |gap| threshold, ~100-140 day-events. Marginal power, disclosed.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead family — and genuinely close: seq 379 month-end MTD-fade (SMV2P slate 2, ~zero, dead-old-regime). Differentiation, per the registry's genuinely-new-hypothesis rule and per the repo's own D3#1 deferral ('needs explicit differentiation, calendar-anchored to quarter only'): (a) signal is stock-MINUS-BOND relative return, not NQ MTD sign — in quarters where stocks and bonds moved together there is no rebalancing flow, and 379's unconditional-sign spec traded all of those no-flow months, plausibly diluting to zero; (b) quarter-anchored with a flow-magnitude threshold (dosage variable of the mechanism itself, not a tuned constant — prereg one threshold, no search); (c) regime structure PREREGISTERED AS RISING (flow proportional to TDF AUM) instead of 379's 'structural or die' gate — dead-old-regime is the mechanism's prediction, not its failure. Honest flag: this is the closest-to-killed proposal in the slate; if the campaign's adjudication reads it as a re-spec of 379, it fails, and that is a legitimate reading — ranked last for exactly this reason. Day-of-week kill: irrelevant (quarter-anchored, flow-motivated). B1: window includes 1-2 overnights; same decomposition arm as TOM-FLOW applies.
proposals.rho_prediction: Predicted near-zero to NEGATIVE losing-day correlation vs Solar — the attractive property: after big up-quarters it is SHORT while a long-biased trend engine is long (anti-correlated exactly when Solar is most extended), and after crash quarters it is long when Solar is likely short/flat. Right-tail: the long side (post-crash quarter-end buying) has violent right-tail upside; the short side into melt-up quarter-ends is the dangerous cell — time-boxed to <= 3 sessions, no stopless open-ended shorts.
proposals.test_design: Frozen spec: signal = QTD NQ total return minus QTD duration-approx bond return (DGS10-based), computed at close of T-3 before quarter-end; if signal > +5% enter SHORT at T-2 RTH close, if < -5% enter LONG; exit at RTH close of first trading day of new quarter (3 sessions max, overnights disclosed); one threshold, no grid. Window 2006-01..2026-05; costs C1. Gates: after-cost net > 0 CI_lo > 0; t_NW >= 2; N >= 30 window-events (power-limited, disclosed — this is a low-N family and cannot clear the campaign's N>=100 day-event convention except by counting day-events ~100-140); WF halves same sign with preregistered second-half-stronger structural prediction; plateau: threshold {4%, 5%, 6%} and entry {T-3, T-2, T-1} all same sign; long-cell and short-cell separately reported, right-tail concentration gates on the short cell; losing-day corr vs Solar <= 0.25 (expected easily met).
proposals.failure_modes: 1) The 379 shadow: its flat result may already BE evidence that index-level rebalancing pressure does not reach NQ — the flow trades ES/SPY/AGG complexes; NDX gets diluted spillover only. 2) Publication decay: HMM published in 2025 and themselves note anticipation shifts the flow earlier — front-running the front-runners compresses exactly the window this spec trades. 3) Free-data dependency may be disallowed — proposal dies at the gate with no fallback. 4) N ~ 30-40 qualifying quarters is thin; a single Mar-2020-type event could dominate the net (top-1% concentration gate per the B02 precedent must apply). 5) Threshold rebalancers trade intra-quarter, not at quarter-end — the calendar anchor may capture only the minority calendar-rebalancer share of the documented flow.

proposals.name: EARN-CAL: mega-cap NDX earnings-night event-risk premium (weight-dose design)
proposals.mechanism: Holding the index through SCHEDULED mega-cap earnings announcements collects a jump-risk premium: investors and dealers de-gross into binary single-name events, and because the top-6 NDX names are now ~45% of the index (vs ~25% in 2006), their scheduled idiosyncratic cash-flow news IS systematic news for NQ. The information hypothesis is an exogenous corporate event calendar (8-K dates), not price state, not directional-change trend capture, not intraday momentum. The dose variable (summed announcing weight per night) gives a mechanism-specific falsifier that no killed family has: if the premium is real it must increase with announcer weight and with the post-2016 concentration regime.
proposals.literature: Stock-level earnings announcement premium: Frazzini & Lamont (NBER 2007); Barber, De George, Lehavy & Trueman, 'The earnings announcement premium around the globe' (JFE 2013, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X12002188) — robust internationally; Savor & Wilson, 'Earnings announcements and systematic risk' (JF 2016, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jofi.12361) — announcers earn ~9.9% annualized abnormal, risk-based (covariance with market cash-flow news spikes at announcement, i.e., a compensated premium, not a mispricing). Earnings JUMP risk is priced (options evidence): Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck & Seeger, 'Option pricing of earnings announcement risks' (2019). CRITICAL adverse evidence I verified: Heitz, Narayanamoorthy & Zekhnini, 'The Disappearing Earnings Announcement Premium' (SSRN 3296537, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3296537) — US cross-sectional premium disappeared after the 2004 8-K disclosure regulation (sample 1994-2016), though it remains robust internationally. Their sample ENDS exactly where the NDX concentration regime begins; the index-level, mega-cap-concentration transfer 2016-2026 is untested in the literature in either direction. No paper documents an index-level mega-cap announcement-night premium — this proposal is explicitly a transfer test, not a replication.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO pays: portfolio managers and dealers who systematically cut gross exposure into binary mega-cap events (career/VaR risk on a scheduled date) and repurchase after — insurance-style flow that persists because it is a knowing risk transfer, not an arbitrageable mistake (Savor-Wilson's risk-based reading). In options space the same event risk is demonstrably priced at 1-2%/event in mega-cap names; the question is whether any delta-1 shadow of it survives at the index. Persistence argument: compensated event risk does not decay the way mispricings do — but HNZ's US evidence says the stock-level directional drift component did decay post-2004, so the honest prior is a small or zero effect.
proposals.implementability: Fully implementable today with zero paid data. Events: SEC EDGAR 8-K item 2.02 acceptance timestamps (free, scriptable) for the top-8 NDX weights per calendar year, 2006-2026; year-start constituent-weight lists frozen from public snapshots and committed BEFORE any outcome is read. Returns: NQ 1-min 2006-01..2026-05 (6.47M bars) covers every event window including the 16:00-17:00 and 18:00+ Globex segments where announcements land. Expected N≈550-650 event-nights after merging same-night announcers. Calendar-integrity risk (AM/PM misclassification = lookahead) mitigated by using 8-K acceptance timestamps and a volume-spike QC cross-check used for auditing only, never selection.
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead families, all mechanically distinct: (1) post-macro-release drift (SMV2X seq 397, flat) — that was reaction-following after 08:30/14:00 MACRO releases; this holds through a corporate calendar event, a different exogenous calendar and a premium-collection (not continuation) hypothesis; (2) B1 overnight long premium (PARKED, not proposable) — B1 is every-night generic inventory premium; this selects ~35 nights/yr by an exogenous corporate calendar, disjoint information class; (3) shock-day continuation (SMV2X, killed) — that conditioned ex-post on realized 3-sigma shocks; this conditions ex-ante on a schedule; (4) pre-FOMC (closed permanently) — macro calendar, different family. Verified by grep: the strings 'earnings', 'Savor', 'Frazzini' appear NOWHERE in research/ — this data class has never been touched by any of the ~40 closed families. It is not OHLCV feature mining (kill-listed): the signal is an external calendar, not a bar-derived feature.
proposals.rho_prediction: Losing-day correlation vs Solar predicted ≈0.00-0.10: exposure is ~35 nights/year (≈14% of sessions), and the repo's own measured priors for sparse overnight sleeves are corr 0.015 (B1) and 0.066-0.104 (c01_t07 conditional sleeve). Conditional on a shared night where NQ gaps down and Solar is long, both lose — so the corr gate must be measured on the full daily ledger, which the sparsity keeps ≤0.25 unless the effect is degenerate.
proposals.test_design: FROZEN before any outcome read: (a) universe = top-8 NDX weights at each calendar-year start (public snapshots, list committed first); (b) event = 8-K item 2.02 earnings date; after-close announcers: long 1 NQ at the 15:55 ET bar close announcement day, exit 09:35 ET bar close next RTH day; before-open announcers: entry prior day 15:55, exit announcement day 10:00; same-night announcers merged, weight summed; (c) costs $4.36/RT + 1 tick/side = $14.36/event; (d) PRIMARY gate: weighted-dose regression net_return_i = a + b*w_i, H1 b>0 with Newey-West t>=2, AND pooled net mean of the top-decile-weight events >0 with CI_lo>0 at C1; (e) SECONDARY preregistered directional prediction (a prediction, not an excuse): 2006-2015 effect <= 2016-2026 effect, stated BEFORE the read so late-sample concentration is a mechanism confirmation rather than a 2026-stub-style artifact — with the explicit rule that if the edge exists ONLY in a <=2-year terminal stub it fails regardless; (f) split-half sign agreement, LOYO by year, no single event >15% of net, losing-day corr vs Solar daily ledger <=0.25; (g) kill rule: dose-slope t<1 or top-decile pooled mean <=0 closes the family permanently; the calendar is retained as infrastructure either way.
proposals.failure_modes: 1) Power is the honest killer: at an 11% announcer weight, even a 50bp underlying event premium is ~5-6bp of NQ (~$230) against per-event sigma of $3,700-7,000 — the binary-mean test needs ~17bp/event for t=2 at N=160 top-weight events; the dose-regression pools all ~600 events and the weight variation to partially rescue this, but an honest expected outcome is underpowered-null. 2) HNZ document the US stock-level premium as GONE post-2004 — the proposal survives only if index-level concentration-era dynamics differ, which is exactly the untested claim. 3) Fat left tail per event: a mega-cap miss gaps NQ 1.5-3% overnight (worst plausible ~5% = $23k/contract on NQ; test measures NQ economics, any live expression would start MNQ-sized) — one bad night can dominate a year, hence the 15%-of-net single-event gate. 4) Calendar-construction lookahead risk (mitigated as described). 5) If the premium exists but loads only on NVDA 2023-2026, it is a 1-name story indistinguishable from a stub — the LOYO and single-event gates are designed to catch precisely that. Residual value on failure: the first exogenous corporate-event data class in the repo, immediately reusable to MEASURE (not yet act on) the incumbent's realized exposure through mega-cap earnings nights — an event-risk audit the program has never run.

proposals.name: PREHOL: pre-holiday session long (exchange-closure inventory/mood premium) — designated cheap kill
proposals.mechanism: The trading session immediately before a multi-day exchange closure historically carries abnormally high returns: shorts reduce exposure ahead of un-hedgeable closure gap risk and financing over the closure (buy-to-cover flow), market makers flatten inventory, and retail mood buying adds a bid. Calendar-anchored, flow-driven, one day of exposure ~9-10 times/year — mechanically unrelated to directional-change trend capture, intraday momentum, or any price-state trigger.
proposals.literature: Ariel (JF 1990): US index pre-holiday returns 9-14x ordinary days, 1963-1982, independent of other calendar effects. Lakonishok & Smidt (RFS 1988): 90 years of DJIA, pre-holiday 0.22%/day vs 0.0094%. Futures-specific: Fabozzi, Ma & Briley, 'Holiday trading in futures markets' (JF 49(1) 1994, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1994.tb04432.x): significantly higher pre-holiday futures returns, strongest for exchange-closed holidays, consistent with inventory adjustment. DECAY (verified, decisive for the prior): Ko & Yang, 'The Pre-Holiday Premium of Ariel (1990) Has Largely Become a Small-Firm Effect Out of Sample' (Critical Finance Review 13(3-4) 2024, https://www.emerald.com/cfr/article/13/3-4/531/1326451): 1983-2019, effect survives ONLY in small firms; insignificant for large firms especially post-1990. Chong, Hudson, Keasey & Littler (JIMF 2005, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0261560605000938): US decline, 1991-97 reversal. Dzhabarov & Ziemba (JPM 2010, https://jpm.pm-research.com/content/36/3/93.abstract): in S&P/Russell FUTURES 1993-2009 a residual persists but is much weaker and concentrated around T-3, stronger in small-caps.
proposals.economic_driver: WHO pays: short-side traders buying to cover ahead of closure gap risk (Chen & Singal JF 2003 documents the analogous weekend short-covering channel — extension to holidays is inference, flagged as such) and liquidity demanders trading into a thinning pre-holiday book. To the extent a residual survives, it persists because per-event capacity (~10 days/yr, one contract-scale flow) is below institutional interest. The honest prior from Ko-Yang is that on a MEGA-CAP index this driver no longer clears zero.
proposals.implementability: Trivial — an afternoon of work, zero new data. Holiday calendar derivable from the NQ 1-min file itself (missing full sessions 2006-2026) cross-checked against CME notices; ~195-205 events including Juneteenth from 2022. Early-close pre-holiday sessions (July 3, Christmas Eve) handled by exiting at the session's actual last RTH bar, a convention the repo already handles deterministically (43 known half-days).
proposals.overlap_check: Closest dead families: day-of-week (closed) — a different, non-overlapping calendar partition; month-end flow (SMV2P, killed ~zero) — month-turn rebalancing, no holiday overlap in mechanism or dates except incidental; weekend information-diffusion (slate 5, flat) — tested Monday continuation of Friday consensus, not a pre-closure premium; overnight drift (killed) — every-night premium, not calendar-selected; opex/post-expiration (killed) — expiration calendar, disjoint. Verified by grep: no holiday-ANOMALY test exists anywhere in research/ (all 'holiday' hits are session-template handling). The frozen S2 closure covers clock-of-day windows for Solar eligibility, not standalone calendar-day engines. This is the last never-tested cell of the calendar axis.
proposals.rho_prediction: Losing-day correlation vs Solar predicted ≈0: ~10 exposure days/year (≈4% of sessions) mechanically bounds daily-ledger correlation near zero; the repo's sparse-sleeve priors (0.015-0.104) apply a fortiori. Trivially right-tail-safe for the incumbent (fully standalone, no overlay).
proposals.test_design: FROZEN: events = all CME full-closure US holidays 2006-01..2026-05. PRIMARY: long 1 NQ from T-2 session's last RTH bar close (15:55 ET or early-close equivalent) to T-1 (pre-holiday) session's last RTH bar close. SECONDARY (Dzhabarov-Ziemba-motivated, Bonferroni-2): the same trade at T-3→T-2. Costs $14.36/event. Gates: pooled net mean CI_lo>0 at C1 with NW t>=2 (after Bonferroni), >=60% of years positive, split-half same sign, no single holiday-type >50% of net, losing-day corr vs Solar ledger <=0.25. Power: N≈200 detects a >=0.18% mean at t≈2 — fully powered against the HISTORICAL effect (0.22-0.36%), honestly underpowered against a decayed residual <0.1%. Kill rule: failure closes the NQ calendar-anomaly axis permanently (joining day-of-week and month-end), which is itself the deliverable.
proposals.failure_modes: 1) The best out-of-sample replication (Ko-Yang 2024) says the large-cap effect is gone post-1990 — expected outcome is NULL; this is proposed as a designated cheap kill (an established repo category, cf. the overnight-drift and NDX-rebalance kills), not a conviction candidate. 2) Left tail is real and in-window: 2018-12-24 (Christmas Eve, S&P -2.7%) is a pre-holiday session the frozen test will eat — correctly. 3) Small N caps any claim: even a pass at t≈2 on N≈200 with a decayed-lit prior deserves a discounted posterior and would need the T-3 secondary and holiday-type robustness to agree before any promotion talk. 4) Back-adjusted continuous contract damps early-year log returns — run the test in point/dollar space (repo convention, already documented in c01_t07).

verdicts.name: CLOSEREV (auction-close)
verdicts.reason: Virgin window verified (16:00-16:14 never traded by any engine or dead family; H6 ranked #9 in DR_V2_PASS_A and never consumed); fresh JFM 2023 literature with a falsifiable era-trend prediction; arithmetic plausible: on |z|>=2 days a 30-60pt impulse reverting even 15% in 14min = 4.5-9 pts vs ~1-1.5pt realistic all-in cost, N~115-250 events gives t~2.3 at a 3bp effect — marginal but testable, and the preregistered BBO slippage audit converts the thin-book objection into a measured pre-outcome kill switch.

verdicts.name: EODREV (auction-close)
verdicts.reason: Its long cell is a re-conditioned neighbor of tested-and-killed seq 370 (registry shows the CONDITIONAL post-down-day overnight long was already ~zero, which the proposal's overlap check misstates as 'unconditional'); the premise is contested in print (Ivanov-Lenkey: LETF impact economically insignificant after controls), the adjacent Gao effect has documented post-publication death, and fading large down days overnight is short-crash-insurance — the tail gate would do all the work on a mechanism with a bad prior.

verdicts.name: LIQREV-1 (liquidity-cycles)
verdicts.reason: Strongest literature in the slate (Nagel RFS 2012 conditionality, CGW QJE 1993 index-level, Brunnermeier-Pedersen persistence mechanism); cost hurdle trivial (0.31bp vs a claimed 5-10bp conditional effect); N>=300 across 8 stress clusters fixes the 2022-26-only sample flaw of the dead fades; calm-state placebo is a genuine built-in falsifier; and the repo's own measured complementarity paradox (fades +$306/+$401 on champion bottom-decile days, corr -0.11) is direct local corroboration of the state-dependence claim.

verdicts.name: LIQSTATE-0 (liquidity-cycles)
verdicts.reason: Not an engine and cannot clear the frozen bar (positive after-cost standalone expectancy) by construction — a legitimate, cheap, well-designed infrastructure study whose own most-likely outcome (NQ spread pinned at 1 tick, proxies collapse to noisy realized-vol) it honestly states; approve as a side-task if capacity exists, but it does not merit a lane candidate slot.

verdicts.name: TOM-FLOW (calendar-flow)
verdicts.reason: Differentiation from killed seq 379 verified in the registry (379 was a conditional last-2-day MTD-sign FADE; this is always-long T-1..T+3) and the repo's own D3#3 deferral condition (zero-correlation check vs the killed signal) is preregistered; cost is negligible for a 4-day hold, N~245 window events, and the full historical effect (0.47%/window vs ~2.8% window sigma) gives pooled t~2.6 — decisive and cheap, though a 50% post-1990 decay (Maberly-Waggoner) drops t to ~1.3 and kills it, and its long-only beta gives it the worst correlation character of the surviving set.

verdicts.name: TERMFLOW (calendar-flow)
verdicts.reason: The repo's own DR_V4 pass rated exactly this 'strong candidate, low dedup' and designated it the next step if 398 failed (398 failed on the N gate) — so the intraday-momentum-mask worry is answered by the repo's prior dedup adjudication plus the preregistered flagged-minus-matched-unflagged gate that prevents re-expressing MOM01's null; power is real (~600 events, a 5bp flagged-day effect vs ~30bp 10-min sigma gives t~4), but the direction proxy (no imbalance feed) and the sign ambiguity in its own citations (B-M near-complete reversion) rank it last among survivors.

verdicts.name: QREBAL (calendar-flow)
verdicts.reason: Power arithmetic is fatal and foreordained: N~30-40 qualifying quarter-events with Harvey et al's ~17bp pressure vs ~2.5% 3-session sigma gives t~0.4 (even 3x the published effect gives t~1.2), so the preregistered t_NW>=2 gate cannot plausibly be reached; add the out-of-substrate bond-leg dependency (no fallback by its own admission) and the repo-adjudicated 'moderate dedup vs killed 379' and this is an un-runnable proposal, not a weak one.

verdicts.name: EARN-CAL (wildcard)
verdicts.reason: Novelty verified (earnings/Savor/Frazzini appear nowhere in research/) and the calendar is genuinely exogenous, but the proposal's own arithmetic concedes the kill: ~5-6bp of NQ per event (~$230) vs $3,700-7,000 per-event sigma needs ~17bp for t=2 at N=160 top-decile events, and the best US out-of-sample evidence (Heitz et al: stock-level premium gone post-2004) says the true effect is likely smaller still — an honest expected underpowered-null with a fat single-night left tail; fund the free EDGAR calendar as infrastructure if desired, not the engine bet.

verdicts.name: PREHOL (wildcard)
verdicts.reason: No repo collision (verified: registry 'holiday' hits are all session-handling, not alpha), but the proposal's own decisive citation kills it before the test runs: Ko-Yang CFR 2024 shows the pre-holiday premium survives ONLY in small firms and is insignificant for large caps post-1990 — NDX is the extreme opposite case — and at ~200 events a plausible residual of 0-5bp vs 130bp daily sigma gives t~0.5; running a documented modern null on a mega-cap index is a mis-spend even as a 'designated cheap kill'.

ranked_candidates.name: LIQREV-1 (stress-gated daily-horizon liquidity-provision reversal)
ranked_candidates.why: Best combination of literature depth, cost headroom, power, falsifiability, and — decisively — correlation character. The literature is top-tier and mechanism-specific (Nagel RFS 2012 shows the reversal premium is a liquidity-provision return that spikes precisely when intermediary capital withdraws; CGW QJE 1993 is index-level, time-series evidence, the exact object being traded; Brunnermeier-Pedersen explains why it cannot be arbitraged flat). The cost arithmetic is the most forgiving in the slate: $14.36/RT is 0.31bp of notional against a claimed conditional effect of 5-10bp, so the test is purely an existence question. Power is adequate (N>=300 events across 8 named stress clusters over 20 years — a 4x larger stress sample than any dead fade test, which were all 2022-26-only). The design contains the slate's best falsifier: the calm-state placebo must be ~zero or the family self-terminates, which cleanly separates 'stress-conditional liquidity premium' from 'generic reversion,' the class the repo has rightly buried. Most importantly for the program's actual need, the repo's own measured evidence (COMPLEMENTARY_ENGINE_FRONTIER lines 31-33: fades earn +$306/+$401 on champion bottom-decile days with losing-day corr -0.11) already demonstrates the diversification direction exists on exactly these days — what died before was unconditional expectancy, which is precisely what the stress gate is hypothesized to fix. Main risks (cascade left tail, index-level transfer from cross-sectional constructions, 2022-26 reversion-hostile regime) are each covered by a specific preregistered gate rather than by hope.

ranked_candidates.name: CLOSEREV (post-close cash-close price-pressure reversion, 16:00-16:14 ET)
ranked_candidates.why: The only proposal exploiting a genuinely virgin window — verified against the repo: no engine, no dead family, and no scalping-lab zone has ever traded 16:00-16:14, and the repo's own deep-research pass ranked this hypothesis (H6) but never consumed it. Literature is fresh and specific (Bogousslavsky-Muravyev JFM 2023) with an unusual asset: a structural falsifier (closing-auction share tripled 2010-2018, so the effect must be non-decreasing across eras — the opposite signature of the campaign's dead-old-regime failures). The arithmetic is marginal but honest: index-level netting means the tradable events are the |z|>=2 tail (~115-250 events over 20 years), and a 15% reversion of a 30-60pt impulse (4.5-9 pts) clears a realistic 1-1.5pt all-in cost 3-6x, giving t~2.3 at a 3bp net effect. Two design features earn the rank: the preregistered BBO slippage audit on the tick year turns the thin-post-close-book objection into a measured pre-outcome kill, and the impulse-proportional stop plus event-loss atlas addresses the 16:05 mega-cap earnings contamination explicitly. The six-fade graveyard is a real prior against any NQ reversion, but every dead fade was structure-anchored and intraday-RTH; a scheduled-flow anchor in a never-traded segment is the one reversion form that prior does not actually cover.

ranked_candidates.name: TOM-FLOW (turn-of-month institutional cash-cycle long window)
ranked_candidates.why: The deepest and oldest literature in the slate (Lakonishok-Smidt 90 years, McConnell-Xu with futures confirmation, Etula et al RFS 2020 for the mechanism) and the cheapest decisive test: pure day-of-month flags on the existing substrate, N~245 window events, and cost that is negligible for a 4-day hold in every era. Differentiation from killed seq 379 verified in the registry (379 was a conditional sign-flipping 2-day MTD fade; this is unconditional always-long with 3 of 4 days non-overlapping), and the repo's own deferral condition — an explicit zero-correlation check vs the killed signal — is preregistered, as is the B1-overnight-decomposition auto-fail rule, which is the most honest self-kill clause in the slate. Ranked below the top two for three reasons: (1) the decisive literature dispute (Maberly-Waggoner: dead in S&P futures post-1990; Dzhabarov-Ziemba: alive but migrated) means the modern-era prior is genuinely 50/50, and at half the historical effect the pooled t drops to ~1.3 and fails; (2) power is therefore knife-edge rather than comfortable; (3) it has the worst correlation character of the survivors — unhedged long beta 4 days a month vs a long-biased trend engine, with crash-month TOM windows the exact cell where the rho<=0.25 gate and the left tail both bind.

ranked_candidates.name: TERMFLOW (calendar-flagged terminal-flow continuation into the cash close)
ranked_candidates.why: Survives primarily because the repo already adjudicated it: DR_V4 pass D3#2 rated the standalone terminal-flow candidate 'strong candidate, low dedup' and deferred it to a future slate conditional on 398 failing — 398 failed on the N gate, making this the repo's own designated next step rather than a scout's resurrection of intraday momentum. The flagged-minus-matched-unflagged control gate is the correct design to prevent re-expressing MOM01's clean null, and the power arithmetic works at literature effect sizes (~600 events; a 5bp flagged-day drift vs ~30bp 10-min sigma gives t~4, and even 2bp gives t~1.6). Ranked last of the candidates because three compounding weaknesses could each halve the realized effect: the direction proxy (15:30-15:50 move standing in for an imbalance feed we do not have), the sign ambiguity in its own citations (Bogousslavsky-Muravyev document near-complete reversion of auction deviations, so the final-minutes segment may be fade-shaped rather than continuation-shaped), and the early-era cost squeeze (0.72 pts was ~4.5bp of 2006 NQ, eating most of a 'several bp' drift in the first half of the walk-forward). A significantly negative result would still be information, but the prior on the positive continuation sign is the shakiest of the four survivors.

gate.best: LIQREV-1 (stress-gated daily-horizon liquidity-provision reversal). It has the highest joint probability of (a) the effect existing, (b) the test detecting it, and (c) the result being the complement the program actually needs — an engine that earns on the snapback/whipsaw days where the Solar trend family gives back, with in-repo measured corroboration (-0.11 losing-day corr, +$306/+$401 on champion bottom-decile days) that the diversification direction is real and only unconditional expectancy was missing. EXACT PREREGISTERED TEST (freeze in runs/<id>/spec.yaml before any outcome read): Substrate = daily RTH ledger built from NQ 1-min, 2006-01-03..2026-05, roll days skipped. State variable = trailing 5-day realized vol (from 1-min RTH returns) >= 90th percentile of trailing 252 sessions. Trigger = session close-to-close return in the bottom quintile (enter LONG) or top quintile (enter SHORT) of the trailing 63 sessions, evaluated only when state=stress. Execution = enter 15:58 ET at market, exit next session 15:58 ET (1-day hold primary; 2-day hold as one plateau axis), 1 contract, no intraday stop, long and short cells reported separately. Costs = $4.36/RT + 1 tick per side ($14.36/RT).
